metadata.title: Mid-Semester Internal Assessment – Distributed Memory Programming with MPI
metadata.instructions: Answer all questions. Write clearly and show any required steps. Marks are allocated as indicated. Use only concepts covered in the course syllabus and lecture material.

questions.question_text: List three MPI functions that are typically used for collective communication in distributed‑memory programs. Briefly state the purpose of each function.
questions.answer_key:
1. MPI_Bcast – broadcasts a message from one process to all other processes in a communicator.
2. MPI_Reduce – combines values from all processes using a specified operation (e.g., sum, max) and returns the result to the root process.
3. MPI_Gather – collects data from all processes and assembles it in order at the root process.
(Each function description worth 1.5 marks; correct identification of three functions worth 0.5 mark.)

questions.question_text: You are required to compute the definite integral of a function f(x) over the interval [a, b] using the trapezoidal rule on a distributed‑memory system with MPI. Outline a step‑by‑step algorithm that (a) partitions the interval among processes, (b) uses an appropriate MPI collective operation to combine the partial results, and (c) describes how you would evaluate the performance of your implementation (mention at least two metrics).
questions.answer_key:
Algorithm (≈3 marks):
1. Each process computes its local sub‑interval: 
   - Determine the number of trapezoids n per process (e.g., total N divided by number of processes).
   - Compute local start = a + rank * (b‑a)/size and local end = start + (b‑a)/size.
2. Each process applies the trapezoidal rule on its sub‑interval to obtain a local integral value.
3. Use MPI_Reduce with MPI_SUM (or MPI_Allreduce) to combine all local integrals into the global integral at the root process.
4. Root process outputs the final integral.

Performance evaluation (≈2 marks):
- Measure execution time for varying numbers of processes and compute speedup = T_serial / T_parallel.
- Compute efficiency = speedup / number_of_processes.
(Additional acceptable metrics: communication overhead, scalability.)

Marking scheme: correct partitioning (1 mark), correct use of MPI_Reduce/Allreduce (1 mark), clear description of performance metrics (1 mark), overall clarity and completeness (2 marks).
